name: Push-Up

instructions.setup: Place hands slightly wider than shoulder-width on the floor, feet together, creating a straight line from head to heels.
execution: Lower your body by bending elbows until chest nearly touches the floor.
Keep elbows at a 45-degree angle to your torso.
Push back up to the starting position by extending arms fully.
tips: Engage glutes and core to prevent lower back sagging.
Maintain a neutral neck position looking slightly ahead of your hands.

description: The fundamental horizontal pushing exercise for developing upper body strength and stability.

name: Pull-Up

instructions.setup: Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
execution: Hang with arms fully extended in a dead hang.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving elbows down.
Continue until your chin is over the bar.
Lower yourself with control.
tips: Avoid using momentum or 'kipping'.
Keep your core tight to prevent swinging.

description: The gold standard for upper body pulling strength and back width.

name: Bodyweight Squat

instructions.setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out.
execution: Lower your hips back and down as if sitting in a chair.
Keep your chest up and knees tracking over toes.
Descend until thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to return to standing.
tips: Keep your weight distributed through the whole foot.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.

description: The basic lower body movement for building leg foundation.

name: Parallel Bar Dip

instructions.setup: Support your body on parallel bars with arms locked out.
execution: Lower your body by bending elbows until shoulders are below elbow height.
Lean slightly forward to engage the chest more.
Push back up to the starting position.
tips: Keep elbows tucked close to the body or at a 45-degree angle.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders at the top.

description: A powerful vertical pushing exercise for the triceps and chest.

name: Inverted Row

instructions.setup: Lie under a low bar, grasp it with an overhand grip, and keep your body in a straight line.
execution: Pull your chest to the bar by retracting your shoulder blades.
Keep the core tight and body rigid.
Lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
tips: The lower the bar, the harder the exercise.
Focus on squeezing the shoulder blades together at the top.

description: A horizontal pulling exercise essential for posture and back thickness.

name: Diamond Push-Up

instructions.setup: Place hands together under your chest so thumbs and index fingers form a diamond shape.
execution: Lower your chest until it touches the back of your hands.
Keep elbows close to your ribs.
Push back up to full extension.
tips: If it hurts your wrists, slightly separate your hands.
Maintain a solid plank position.

description: A push-up variation that emphasizes the triceps.

name: Hanging Leg Raise

instructions.setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width grip.
execution: Keeping legs straight, raise them until they are parallel to the floor or higher.
Slowly lower them back down without swinging.
tips: To reduce difficulty, perform with bent knees (Knee Raises).
Exhale as you lift the legs.

description: One of the most effective exercises for developing core strength and hip flexor control.

name: Pike Push-Up

instructions.setup: Start in a push-up position, then walk feet forward until your body forms an inverted V-shape.
execution: Lower your head forward toward the floor to form a tripod shape with your hands.
Push back up to the pike position.
tips: Look at your feet to maintain a neutral neck.
Keep your hips high throughout the movement.

description: The primary bodyweight progression toward the handstand push-up.

name: Pistol Squat

instructions.setup: Stand on one leg with the other leg extended straight out in front.
execution: Lower your hips down as far as possible on the standing leg.
Keep the extended leg off the ground.
Drive back up to a standing position.
tips: Use a pole or TRX for assistance if you lack balance.
Work on ankle mobility if your heel lifts off the floor.

description: An advanced single-leg exercise that requires strength, balance, and mobility.

name: Chin-Up

instructions.setup: Grasp the bar with an underhand grip (palms facing you), shoulder-width apart.
execution: Pull your body up until your chin is above the bar.
Keep elbows close to your body.
Lower yourself back to a full hang.
tips: Focus on pulling with the biceps as well as the back.
Maintain a full range of motion.

description: A pull-up variation that puts more emphasis on the biceps.

name: Wide Grip Pull-Up

instructions.setup: Grasp the bar with an overhand grip significantly wider than shoulder-width.
execution: Pull your chest toward the bar.
Lower back down with control.
tips: Do not go too wide, as it can cause shoulder impingement.
Focus on driving the elbows down into your sides.

description: Increases the demand on the lats by reducing the mechanical advantage of the arms.

name: Muscle-Up

instructions.setup: Grasp the bar with a false grip (if possible) or a standard overhand grip.
execution: Perform an explosive pull-up, pulling the bar to your lower chest/waist.
Lean your torso forward over the bar to transition from pull to push.
Press your body up until arms are fully extended (dip).
tips: Requires a high level of pulling and dipping power.
The transition is the most difficult part of the movement.

description: The ultimate calisthenics skill combining a pull-up and a dip.

name: Archer Push-Up

instructions.setup: Place hands very wide, with one arm acting as the primary mover and the other kept straight.
execution: Lower your body toward the primary hand while the auxiliary arm slides out straight.
Push back up to the center.
Switch sides or alternate.
tips: Keep the straight arm as straight as possible.
This is a great progression for the one-arm push-up.

description: A unilateral push-up variation that builds immense chest and tricep strength.

name: Pseudo Planche Push-Up

instructions.setup: In a push-up position, turn your hands slightly outward and lean your shoulders forward past your hands.
execution: Maintain the forward lean while lowering your chest.
Push back up while keeping the lean consistent.
tips: The further you lean forward, the harder the exercise.
Keep your protraction (rounded upper back) at the top.

description: Mimics the planche position to build specific shoulder strength.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat

instructions.setup: Place one foot behind you on a bench and the other foot forward.
execution: Lower your hips until your front thigh is parallel to the ground.
Keep your torso upright.
Push back to the start using the front leg.
tips: Ensure your front foot is far enough forward to keep the knee from overextending.
Focus on balance and control.

description: An excellent unilateral leg exercise for correcting imbalances.

name: Glute Bridge

instructions.setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
execution: Lift your hips toward the ceiling while squeezing your glutes.
Hold for a second at the top.
Lower back down slowly.
tips: Drive through your heels.
Don't overarch your lower back.

description: A fundamental glute activation and strengthening exercise.

name: Hollow Body Hold

instructions.setup: Lie on your back with arms extended overhead and legs straight.
execution: Lift your legs and upper back off the floor, keeping your lower back pressed firmly into the ground.
Hold this 'banana' shape.
tips: If your lower back arches, lift your legs higher or bend your knees.
Focus on creating maximal tension in the core.

description: The foundational core position for all calisthenics skills.

name: L-Sit

instructions.setup: Support your weight on your hands with arms locked out.
execution: Lift your legs until they are parallel to the floor, forming an L-shape.
Keep your shoulders depressed and chest up.
tips: If straight legs are too hard, start with a tucked L-sit.
Focus on pushing the floor away.

description: A static hold that builds incredible core and tricep compression strength.

name: Wall Walk

instructions.setup: Start in a push-up position with your feet against a wall.
execution: Walk your feet up the wall while walking your hands toward the wall.
End in a stomach-to-wall handstand.
Reverse the movement back to the start.
tips: Keep your core tight to avoid 'banana back'.
Control the movement throughout.

description: A great exercise for shoulder stability and handstand preparation.

name: Calf Raise

instructions.setup: Stand on the edge of a step or on flat ground.
execution: Rise up onto the balls of your feet.
Hold for a second, then lower back down below the level of the step.
tips: Pause at the top and bottom to maximize the stretch and contraction.
Perform one leg at a time to increase difficulty.

description: The standard exercise for building the lower leg muscles.

name: Superman Hold

instructions.setup: Lie face down with arms extended in front and legs straight.
execution: Simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor.
Hold the position while squeezing your glutes and lower back.
tips: Look at the floor to maintain a neutral neck.
Focus on length rather than height.

description: An essential exercise for strengthening the posterior chain and lower back.

name: Cossack Squat

instructions.setup: Stand with a very wide stance.
execution: Shift your weight to one side and squat down while keeping the other leg straight.
The straight leg's toes should point up as you descend.
Push back to the center.
tips: Keep your heel on the floor on the working leg.
Maintain an upright torso.

description: Combines unilateral strength with deep flexibility for the inner thighs.

name: Plank

instructions.setup: Place forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders, feet together.
execution: Hold a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and squeeze your glutes.
tips: Avoid letting your hips sag or hike up.
Think about pulling your elbows toward your toes to engage the core more.

description: The fundamental isometric core stabilization exercise.

name: Side Plank

instructions.setup: Lie on your side with your weight on one forearm and the side of your foot.
execution: Lift your hips to form a straight line.
Hold the position and then switch sides.
tips: Keep your shoulder directly over your elbow.
Don't let your hips drop toward the floor.

description: Target the lateral core and obliques.

name: Mountain Climber

instructions.setup: Start in a high plank position.
execution: Rapidly alternate bringing your knees toward your chest.
Maintain a steady pace and keep your hips low.
tips: Do not bounce your hips.
Focus on speed and core control.

description: A high-intensity exercise for core and cardiovascular health.

name: Burpee

instructions.setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
execution: Drop into a squat, place hands on floor, jump feet back to a push-up position.
Perform a push-up (optional), jump feet forward, and jump explosively into the air.
tips: Maintain a rhythm to manage fatigue.
Focus on explosive movement.

description: The ultimate full-body conditioning exercise.

name: V-Up

instructions.setup: Lie on your back with arms and legs extended.
execution: Simultaneously lift your torso and legs to touch your toes, forming a V-shape.
Lower back down with control.
tips: Try to keep your legs straight.
Exhale as you reach for your toes.

description: An advanced core exercise that targets both upper and lower abs.

name: Jumping Jack

instructions.setup: Stand with feet together and arms at your sides.
execution: Jump while spreading your legs and swinging your arms above your head.
Jump back to the starting position.
tips: Maintain a steady pace.
Stay light on the balls of your feet.

description: A classic warm-up and cardiovascular exercise.

name: Bicycle Crunch

instructions.setup: Lie on your back with hands behind your head and knees bent.
execution: Bring your opposite elbow to your opposite knee while extending the other leg.
Alternate sides in a cycling motion.
tips: Focus on rotation rather than just pulling your head.
Keep your lower back pressed to the floor.

description: One of the best core exercises for targeting the obliques.

name: Bench Dip

instructions.setup: Sit on a bench, place hands next to hips, and move your feet forward.
execution: Lower your hips by bending your elbows.
Push back up to the start.
tips: Keep your back close to the bench.
Extend your legs to make it harder.

description: A beginner-friendly dip variation focused on the triceps.

name: Close Grip Pull-Up

instructions.setup: Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands closer than shoulder-width.
execution: Pull your chest to the bar.
Lower back down with control.
tips: This version increases the range of motion for the lats.
Maintain a tight core.

description: A pull-up variation that challenges the arms and lower lats.

name: Handstand Hold (Against Wall)

instructions.setup: Kick up or walk up into a handstand with your back or stomach toward a wall.
execution: Hold the position while maintaining a straight line.
Push the floor away and keep your core tight.
tips: Focus on shoulder protraction and elevation.
Look at your hands to maintain balance.

description: A fundamental skill for developing overhead pushing strength and balance.

name: Planche Lean

instructions.setup: In a push-up position, protract your shoulder blades (round your upper back).
execution: Lean forward as far as possible while keeping your arms straight.
Hold the position with max tension.
tips: Keep your elbows locked (straight).
The lean determines the intensity.

description: The foundational isometric hold for the planche progression.

name: Scapular Pull-Up

instructions.setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with arms straight.
execution: Using only your shoulder blades, pull them down and back.
Lift your body slightly without bending your elbows.
Lower back to a dead hang.
tips: This is a subtle movement.
Focus on isolating the movement of the shoulder blades.

description: Develops the necessary shoulder blade control for proper pull-up technique.

name: Scapular Push-Up

instructions.setup: Start in a high plank position with arms straight.
execution: Squeeze your shoulder blades together to lower your chest slightly.
Push your shoulder blades apart to return to the start.
Keep your arms straight throughout.
tips: Do not bend your elbows.
Focus on the movement of the shoulder blades.

description: Builds serratus anterior strength and scapular health.

name: Archer Pull-Up

instructions.setup: Grasp the bar with a very wide overhand grip.
execution: Pull yourself toward one hand while keeping the other arm straight.
Return to the start and repeat on the other side.
tips: The straight arm should slide along the bar.
A key progression for the one-arm pull-up.

description: A unilateral pulling exercise that emphasizes one side of the back at a time.

name: Wall Sit

instructions.setup: Lean against a wall and slide down until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
execution: Hold the position for a set amount of time.
Keep your back flat against the wall.
tips: Ensure your knees are directly over your ankles.
Do not rest your hands on your legs.

description: An isometric leg exercise to build quad endurance.

name: Box Jump

instructions.setup: Stand in front of a sturdy box.
execution: Squat slightly and swing your arms to jump onto the box.
Land softly in a squat position.
Step back down.
tips: Focus on landing with your whole foot on the box.
Step down rather than jumping down to protect your joints.

description: A plyometric exercise for developing explosive power in the legs.

name: Hindu Push-Up

instructions.setup: Start in a pike position (hips high).
execution: Lower your head and sweep your chest close to the floor.
Push your chest up toward the ceiling while lowering your hips (upward dog pose).
Push your hips back to the starting pike position.
tips: The movement should be fluid and circular.
Great for shoulder and spine mobility.

description: A dynamic push-up variation that incorporates mobility and strength.

name: Flutter Kicks

instructions.setup: Lie on your back with legs straight and hands under your glutes for support.
execution: Lift your legs slightly and alternate kicking them up and down in a small range.
tips: Keep your lower back pressed to the floor.
Keep your legs straight.

description: A low-impact core exercise for abdominal endurance.

name: Handstand Push-Up (Wall)

instructions.setup: Kick up into a handstand against a wall.
execution: Lower your head toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Push back up until your arms are fully extended.
tips: Maintain a tight core to avoid arching.
The head should go slightly forward of the hands (tripod).

description: The ultimate bodyweight shoulder-pressing exercise.

name: Jump Squat

instructions.setup: Start in a standing position.
execution: Lower into a squat and then jump as high as you can.
Land softly and go straight into the next rep.
tips: Absorb the landing through your whole foot and bend your knees.
Keep the movements explosive.

description: A plyometric variation of the squat for power and heart rate.

name: Negative Pull-Up

instructions.setup: Jump or use a stool to get your chin above the bar.
execution: Lower yourself as slowly as possible until your arms are fully extended.
tips: Aim for a 5-10 second descent.
Maintain control through the entire range of motion.

description: The best way to build the strength needed for a first pull-up.

name: One-Arm Push-Up

instructions.setup: Place one hand on the floor and spread your feet wide for balance.
execution: Lower your body while keeping your torso as level as possible.
Push back to the start.
tips: Squeeze the glutes and core to manage rotation.
Wider feet make it easier.

description: A high-level unilateral push-up requiring immense core stability.

name: Hanging Knee Raise

instructions.setup: Hang from a pull-up bar.
execution: Pull your knees toward your chest.
Lower them back down with control.
tips: Avoid swinging the body.
Focus on curling your pelvis toward your chest.

description: The foundational hanging core exercise.

name: Toes to Bar

instructions.setup: Hang from a pull-up bar.
execution: Keeping legs as straight as possible, swing your feet up to touch the bar.
Lower back down under control.
tips: Engage your lats to help pull your body back as you lift your legs.
Don't use excessive momentum.

description: An advanced dynamic core and pulling exercise.

name: Plank Shoulder Tap

instructions.setup: Start in a high plank position.
execution: Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder.
Keep your hips from rocking.
Repeat with the other hand.
tips: The wider your feet, the easier it is to stay stable.
Minimize hip movement.

description: Develops core stability by removing one point of contact.

name: Single Leg Glute Bridge

instructions.setup: Lie on your back, one foot flat and the other leg extended in the air.
execution: Drive through the heel of the floor foot to lift your hips.
Hold at the top, then lower slowly.
tips: Keep your hips level throughout.
Squeeze the glute hard at the top.

description: Increases intensity on the glutes and hamstrings unilaterally.

name: Barbell Bench Press (Flat)

instructions.setup: Lie on a flat bench. Grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width. Plant your feet firmly on the ground.
execution: Unrack the bar and stabilize it directly over your shoulders.
Retract your shoulder blades into the bench.
Lower the bar under control to the middle of your chest.
Press the bar back up to the starting position, extending the elbows but not locking them out softly.
tips: Keep your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle to your body, not flared out 90 degrees.
Maintain an arch in your lower back, but keep glutes on the bench.

description: The standard compound movement for overall chest development and upper body pushing strength.

name: Barbell Bench Press (Incline)

instructions.setup: Set an adjustable bench to an incline of 30-45 degrees. Lie back and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
execution: Unrack the bar and hold it above your upper chest.
Lower the bar specifically toward the upper portion of your chest, just below the collarbone.
Press the bar vertically back to the starting position.
tips: Do not set the incline too steep, or the load will shift primarily to the Front Delts.
Control the negative to feel the stretch in the upper pectorals.

description: A variation of the bench press that shifts the focus to the clavicular head of the pectoralis major.

name: Barbell Bench Press (Decline)

instructions.setup: Secure your legs in the decline bench rollers. Lie back and grasp the bar.
execution: Unrack the bar and stabilize it.
Lower the bar to the lower part of your chest (sternum level).
Press the weight back up powerfully.
tips: This variation often allows for more weight due to shorter range of motion and mechanical advantage.
Ensure a spotter is present as racking the weight can be difficult.

description: Targets the sternal/abdominal head of the pectoralis major and often reduces shoulder stress compared to flat pressing.

name: Dumbbell Press (Flat)

instructions.setup: Sit on a flat bench with dumbbells resting on your knees. Kick them up to your shoulders as you lie back.
execution: Press the dumbbells up until arms are extended above your chest.
Lower the weights slowly, allowing a deep stretch at the bottom.
Press back up, bringing the dumbbells close together without touching.
tips: Utilize the greater range of motion dumbbells provide compared to a barbell.
Keep your wrists stacked directly over your elbows.

description: A unilateral chest exercise that helps correct muscle imbalances and allows for a greater range of motion.

name: Dumbbell Press (Incline)

instructions.setup: Set bench to 30-45 degrees. Lie back with dumbbells at shoulder height.
execution: Press the weights straight up over your upper chest.
Lower them under control until the hands are near shoulder level.
Drive the weights back up.
tips: Focus on squeezing the upper chest at the top of the movement.
Keep shoulders depressed to avoid upper trap dominance.

description: Isolates the upper pectorals while requiring significant stabilizer muscle engagement.

name: Dumbbell Press (Decline)

instructions.setup: Secure legs in a decline bench. Lie back with dumbbells at chest level.
execution: Press the dumbbells straight up perpendicular to the floor.
Lower them until you feel a stretch in the lower pecs.
Press back to the start.
tips: Be careful getting into position with heavy dumbbells; consider a partner's help.

description: Focuses on the lower pectoral fibers with the freedom of movement provided by dumbbells.

name: Cable Flye (High Pulley)

instructions.setup: Set pulleys to the highest position. Grasp handles and step forward with a staggered stance.
execution: With a slight bend in the elbows, bring your hands together downward toward your waist.
Squeeze the chest hard at the bottom.
Return slowly to the starting position, feeling a stretch across the chest.
tips: Keep your torso upright; leaning too far forward changes the angle of emphasis.
Imagine trying to hug a large tree trunk downwards.

description: An isolation movement performed from a high angle to specifically target the lower sternal fibers of the chest.

name: Cable Flye (Mid Pulley)

instructions.setup: Set pulleys to shoulder height. Grasp handles and step forward.
execution: Bring hands together directly in front of the chest.
Squeeze the pectorals at the center.
Open arms back up horizontally until a stretch is felt.
tips: Maintain a fixed elbow angle throughout the movement; do not press the weight.

description: Targets the chest muscle as a whole, providing constant tension throughout the range of motion.

name: Cable Flye (Low Pulley)

instructions.setup: Set pulleys to the lowest position. Grasp handles with palms facing forward/up.
execution: Bring your hands upward and together to meet at eye level.
Squeeze the upper chest specifically.
Lower strictly under control.
tips: Avoid using body sway or momentum to swing the weight up.
Keep the chest proud and shoulder blades retracted.

description: Specifically targets the clavicular (upper) fibers of the chest by working against gravity in an upward arc.

name: Chest Dips

instructions.setup: Mount the dip bars, supporting your weight with straight arms.
execution: Lean your torso forward significantly (approx 45 degrees).
Lower your body by bending elbows until shoulders are slightly below elbows.
Press back up to the start, maintaining the forward lean.
tips: The forward lean is critical; staying upright shifts focus almost entirely to the triceps.
Avoid rolling shoulders forward at the bottom of the movement.

description: A bodyweight compound movement often called the 'squat for the upper body', excellent for lower chest development.

name: Pec Deck

instructions.setup: Adjust seat height so handles/pads are at chest level. Sit with back flat against the pad.
execution: Push the handles together until they touch in front of you.
Hold the peak contraction for a second.
Return slowly to the starting position without letting the weight stack touch.
tips: Do not overstretch the shoulders at the back of the movement.
Focus on driving with the elbows, not just the hands.

description: A stable machine exercise that isolates the pectoral muscles and removes the need for stabilization.

name: Machine Chest Press

instructions.setup: Adjust seat so handles align with the middle of your chest.
execution: Press the handles forward until arms are extended.
Return slowly to the start position.
Keep your back firmly against the pad throughout.
tips: Great for safely training to failure without a spotter.
Ensure the elbows do not flare excessively high.

description: A machine-based compound movement allowing for heavy loading with high stability.

name: Floor Press

instructions.setup: Lie on the floor inside a rack. Grip the bar as you would for a bench press.
execution: Unrack the bar and lower it until your triceps touch the floor completely.
Pause briefly to break the eccentric-concentric chain.
Explosively press the bar back up.
tips: This limits range of motion, placing high demand on the lockout (triceps) and mid-range chest strength.
Do not bounce your elbows off the floor.

description: A partial range of motion press performed on the floor, often used to improve lockout strength.

name: Landmine Press

instructions.setup: Place one end of a barbell in a landmine base or corner. Hold the other end at shoulder height.
execution: Press the bar upward and forward at a roughly 45-degree angle.
Lean slightly into the press at the top.
Lower under control to the shoulder.
tips: This can be done with one or two hands.
The pressing path is ideal for upper chest recruitment with less shoulder impingement risk.

description: A functional pressing movement that bridges the gap between vertical and horizontal pressing.

name: Weighted Push-Up

instructions.setup: Assume a standard push-up position with a weight plate on your back (or wearing a vest).
execution: Lower your body until the chest nearly touches the floor.
Keep the body in a rigid plank line.
Push forcefully back to the top position.
tips: Ensure the weight is placed on the upper back/scapula area, not the lower back.
Prevent the hips from sagging.

description: A progressed version of the classic calisthenics exercise using external resistance.

name: Smith Machine Press

instructions.setup: Place a flat bench under the Smith Machine bar.
execution: Unlatch the bar and lower it to the chest.
Press the bar up along the fixed vertical path.
Re-latch the bar when the set is complete.
tips: Because the path is fixed, ensure your alignment is perfect before starting to avoid joint stress.
Useful for slow negatives (eccentrics) safely.

description: A guided barbell press that provides stability, allowing focus on muscle contraction over stabilization.

name: Svend Press

instructions.setup: Stand holding a light weight plate pressed between your palms at chest level.
execution: Squeeze your palms together as hard as possible.
Press the plate straight out in front of you while maintaining the squeeze.
Return the plate to your chest.
tips: The weight of the plate matters less than the inward pressure (squeezing) you create.
This is primarily an isometric tension exercise.

description: A constant-tension accessory exercise focusing on the peak contraction of the inner chest.

name: Dumbbell Pullover

instructions.setup: Lie perpendicular across a bench (upper back on bench) holding a dumbbell with both hands above your chest.
execution: Keeping a slight bend in elbows, lower the weight in an arc behind your head.
Lower until a deep stretch is felt in the chest and lats.
Pull the dumbbell back over your chest to the starting position.
tips: To bias the chest, focus on squeezing the pectorals to bring the weight up.
Do not let the hips shoot up; keep them low to maximize the stretch.

description: A unique movement that works both the chest and back, utilizing a pulling motion to stretch the pectorals.

name: Conventional Deadlift

instructions.setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart, mid-foot under the bar. Grip the bar just outside your legs.
execution: Hinge at the hips to grab the bar, keeping your spine neutral.
Engage your lats (pull the slack out of the bar) and drive your shins to the bar.
Push the floor away with your feet while pulling the bar up along your legs.
Lock out hips and knees simultaneously at the top.
tips: Do not hyperextend your back at the top.
Keep the bar in contact with your legs throughout the entire movement.

description: The king of posterior chain exercises, heavily taxing the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings.

name: Sumo Deadlift

instructions.setup: Take a very wide stance with toes pointed out. Grip the bar inside your knees (shoulder-width apart).
execution: Drop your hips down while keeping your chest upright.
Drive your knees out over your toes.
Push effectively through the floor to separate the bar from the ground.
Lock out by thrusting hips forward.
tips: Torso remains much more upright than in conventional deadlifts.
Focus on 'spreading the floor' with your feet.

description: A deadlift variation that shifts load from the lower back to the hips, glutes, and quads.

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row

instructions.setup: Stand holding a barbell with a double overhand grip. Hinge forward until your torso is roughly 45 degrees to parallel.
execution: Pull the bar towards your lower chest or upper abdomen.
Retract your shoulder blades at the top of the movement.
Lower the bar under control to a full stretch.
tips: Avoid using momentum or jerking the torso upward to move the weight.
Keep the core braced to protect the lower back.

description: A foundational back builder that adds thickness to the entire back musculature.

name: Pendlay Row

instructions.setup: Setup similar to a deadlift. The back must be parallel to the floor.
execution: Explosively pull the bar from the floor to your chest/upper abs.
Return the bar fully to the floor after every rep to a dead stop.
Do not raise your torso angle during the pull.
tips: This is a power movement; strictly minimize body english.
If you cannot keep your back parallel, reduce the weight.

description: A strict barbell row performed from a dead stop on the floor for each rep, prioritizing explosive power.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row

instructions.setup: Place one knee and one hand on a flat bench for support. Hold the DB in the free hand.
execution: Pull the dumbbell towards your hip bone (not your shoulder).
Keep the elbow tucked close to the body.
Lower the weight to a deep stretch.
tips: Imagine pulling with your elbow to engage the lats maximally.
Avoid rotating the torso excessively.

description: A unilateral movement allowing for a greater range of motion and isolation of the latissimus dorsi.

name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)

instructions.setup: Sit with knees secured under pads. Grip the bar wider than shoulder-width, palms facing away.
execution: Depress shoulder blades down and back.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest.
Control the ascent back to a full stretch.
tips: Do not lean back excessively to turn it into a row.
Focus on driving elbows down towards the floor.

description: Targets the upper and outer lats, contributing to back width.

name: Lat Pulldown (Narrow/Neutral Grip)

instructions.setup: Attach a V-handle. Sit with knees secured.
execution: Pull the handle down to the middle of your chest.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together hard at the bottom.
Allow a full stretch at the top.
tips: This variation allows for slightly greater range of motion and bicep recruitment.
Keep the chest proud to hit the mid-back.

description: Targets the lats and the mid-back musculature (rhomboids/traps) due to the neutral grip.

name: Lat Pulldown (Underhand/Reverse)

instructions.setup: Grip the bar shoulder-width apart with palms facing you (supinated).
execution: Pull the bar down to the lower chest.
Keep elbows driven down and close to the body.
Return to start under control.
tips: Biases the lower lat fibers and heavily involves the biceps.
Great for those who struggle to feel their lats with a wide grip.

description: A variation that places the biceps in a strong mechanical position and targets the lower lats.

name: T-Bar Row

instructions.setup: Straddle the bar. Hinge at hips to 45 degrees. Grip the handles (or bar) securely.
execution: Retract scapula and pull the weight toward your chest.
Squeeze the upper back at the top.
Lower the weight without rounding the spine.
tips: The fixed path often allows for heavier loading than free barbell rows.
Avoid letting the ego dictate weight; range of motion is key.

description: Excellent for adding thickness to the middle and upper back.

name: Seated Cable Row

instructions.setup: Sit at the machine with feet on the platform, knees slightly bent. Grab the handle.
execution: Keep torso upright. Pull the handle to your abdomen.
Focus on retracting the scapula fully.
Extend arms forward, allowing the lats to stretch, but keep the torso stationary.
tips: Do not swing back and forth to move the weight.
Keep shoulders down (depressed) to avoid overusing upper traps.

description: A stable horizontal pull that effectively targets the mid-back thickness.

name: Face Pull

instructions.setup: Set pulley to face height. Grasp rope with thumbs facing backward (neutral/hammer grip).
execution: Pull the rope towards your face, separating your hands as they near your ears.
Externally rotate your shoulders at the end range (knuckles facing back).
Return slowly.
tips: Do not go too heavy; this is for shoulder health and posture.
Focus on the external rotation component.

description: Crucial for shoulder health, targeting the rear delts and external rotators to counteract slouching.

name: Rack Pull

instructions.setup: Set safety pins in a rack just below or above the knee. Place bar on pins.
execution: Grip the bar and set your back tight (similar to top half of deadlift).
Pull the bar up and lock out hips and upper back.
Lower the bar back to the pins (don't drop it).
tips: Allows for overloading the upper back/traps with weight heavier than a full deadlift.
Be careful not to 'hitch' or ramp the bar up the thighs.

description: A partial deadlift focusing on the lockout portion, heavily overloading the traps and erectors.

name: Back Extension

instructions.setup: Adjust pad to sit just below your hip bone (allows hip flex). Cross arms over chest.
execution: Lower your torso until you feel a stretch in the hamstrings.
Raise your torso back to neutral (straight line).
Squeeze glutes and lower back at the top.
tips: Do not hyperextend (arch) excessively at the top.
To bias glutes, round the upper back slightly. To bias lower back, keep spine neutral.

description: Strengthens the erector spinae and posterior chain without heavy axial loading.

name: Barbell Shrug

instructions.setup: Stand holding a barbell with a double overhand grip, arms fully extended.
execution: Elevate your shoulders straight up towards your ears.
Hold the peak contraction briefly.
Lower the shoulders back down fully.
tips: Do not roll your shoulders; move strictly up and down.
If grip fails, use straps.

description: Isolation exercise for developing the upper trapezius muscles.

name: Good Morning

instructions.setup: Place bar on your upper back (low bar position preferred). Stand hip-width apart.
execution: Hinge at the hips, sending your butt back while keeping legs nearly straight (soft bend).
Lower torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor.
Reverse the motion by driving hips forward to upright.
tips: This is a hinge, not a squat. Knees should not travel forward.
Start light; the lever arm places high stress on the lower back.

description: A posterior chain builder that strengthens the lower back and hamstrings effectively.

name: Barbell Overhead Press

instructions.setup: Rack the bar at chest height. Grip slightly wider than shoulders. Elbows should be slightly in front of the bar.
execution: Brace your core and glutes excessively to prevent lumbar arching.
Press the bar vertically in a straight line, moving your head back slightly to clear the path.
Once the bar passes the forehead, move the head back under the bar (head through the window).
Lock out overhead with shrugged shoulders.
tips: The bar path must be vertical; do not press the bar around your face.
Squeeze glutes to protect the lower back.

description: The primary measure of upper body vertical pushing strength.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Press

instructions.setup: Sit on a bench with back support (or stand). Kick weights up to shoulder height.
execution: Press the weights upward and slightly in toward the center (without touching).
Lower the weights until the dumbbells touch your shoulders or are roughly ear level.
Maintain vertical forearms throughout.
tips: Offers more freedom of movement than a barbell, making it friendlier on the joints.
Do not flare elbows completely out to the sides; keep them slightly tucked (scapular plane).

description: A compound press that demands more stability than the barbell version, excellent for hypertrophy.

name: Arnold Press

instructions.setup: Hold dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing your body (supinated).
execution: Press the weights up while simultaneously rotating your palms outward.
Finish the movement at the top with palms facing away (pronated).
Reverse the rotation on the way down to the starting position.
tips: This increases the time under tension and range of motion for the front delts.
Start with lighter weight as the rotational mechanics can tax the rotator cuff.

description: A rotational pressing variation popularized by Arnold Schwarzenegger to hit all three deltoid heads.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise

instructions.setup: Stand with dumbbells at your sides, slight bend in elbows.
execution: Raise arms out to the sides until elbows are at shoulder height.
Lead the movement with your elbows, not your hands.
Lower under control.
tips: Avoid swinging the torso to generate momentum.
Think about pushing the weights 'out' towards the walls, not just 'up'.

description: The bread-and-butter isolation exercise for building shoulder width (lateral deltoids).

name: Cable Lateral Raise

instructions.setup: Set pulley to the lowest height. Stand sideways to the machine. Grip handle with the far hand.
execution: Raise the cable out and up to shoulder height.
Maintain constant tension on the way down.
Ideally, the cable should run behind your legs to hit the side delt better.
tips: Provides a superior resistance profile compared to dumbbells, as tension is high even at the bottom.
Do not lean away from the stack excessively.

description: A lateral raise variation providing constant tension throughout the entire range of motion.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise

instructions.setup: Stand holding dumbbells in front of your thighs.
execution: Lift the weight straight out in front of you to shoulder height.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly.
tips: Often redundant if you are already doing heavy overhead or bench pressing.
Can be done with a barbell or weight plate as well.

description: Isolates the anterior deltoid.

name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Flye

instructions.setup: Hinge at the hips until torso is nearly parallel to the floor (or lie chest-down on an incline bench).
execution: With a slight elbow bend, raise arms out to the sides in a reverse hugging motion.
Squeeze the back of the shoulders.
Lower without losing tension.
tips: Do not retract the scapula (shoulder blades) excessively; keep the movement in the shoulder joint to isolate rear delts.
Pinkies should lead the movement.

description: Targets the often-neglected posterior deltoids, crucial for posture and 3D shoulder look.

name: Upright Row

instructions.setup: Hold bar with a shoulder-width grip (avoid very narrow grips).
execution: Pull the bar straight up the body by driving elbows high and out.
Stop when elbows reach shoulder height (chest level).
Lower under control.
tips: Going too high (chin level) with a narrow grip is a primary cause of shoulder impingement.
Use a wider grip to bias the side delts and reduce joint stress.

description: Builds the 'yoke' (traps and side delts), but requires careful form to avoid injury.

name: Push Press

instructions.setup: Same setup as a strict overhead press.
execution: Initiate with a shallow dip of the knees (keep torso upright).
Explosively drive through the legs to launch the bar off the shoulders.
Press out the remainder of the rep with the arms.
tips: Use the legs to generate momentum; the arms finish the movement.
Allows for heavier loads than a strict press, overloading the lockout phase.

description: An explosive power movement that utilizes leg drive to press heavy loads overhead.

name: Cuban Press

instructions.setup: Stand holding light dumbbells in front of thighs.
execution: Phase 1: Perform a wide upright row until elbows are at 90 degrees/shoulder height.
Phase 2: Externally rotate the arms upward (scarecrow position).
Phase 3: Press the weight overhead.
Reverse strictly through all three phases.
tips: Use extremely light weight.
Excellent warm-up or rehab exercise for rotator cuff stability.

description: A complex three-part movement specifically designed to strengthen the rotator cuff and stabilizers.

name: Lu Raise

instructions.setup: Stand with light plates or dumbbells.
execution: Perform a lateral raise, but instead of stopping at shoulder height, continue lifting.
Rotate the scapula and bring the weights all the way until they touch overhead.
Lower under control through the full arc.
tips: Requires good shoulder mobility.
Heavily recruits the traps at the top of the movement, unlike standard lateral raises.

description: A full range-of-motion raise popularized by Olympic weightlifters (Lu Xiaojun) for shoulder stability and mass.

name: Machine Lateral Raise

instructions.setup: Adjust seat height so your shoulder aligns with the machine's pivot point.
execution: Place arms against the pads.
Raise elbows out and up to shoulder level.
Lower slowly.
tips: Strictly removes the ability to 'cheat' with body momentum.
Perfect for drop sets and training to failure safely.

description: A machine isolation movement that enforces strict form and constant tension on the side delts.

name: Barbell Back Squat

instructions.setup: Place bar on upper traps (high bar) or rear delts (low bar). Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
execution: Brace core firmly (Valsalva maneuver).
Break at the hips and knees simultaneously to descend.
Keep knees tracking over toes.
Descend until thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive back up, keeping the chest high.
tips: Do not let knees cave inward (valgus collapse).
Keep the weight over the mid-foot, not the toes or heels.

description: The definitive lower body compound movement for overall mass and strength.

name: Barbell Front Squat

instructions.setup: Rack the bar across your front delts, securing it with a 'clean grip' or crossed arms. Elbows must be high.
execution: Descend vertically. The torso must remain much more upright than in a back squat.
Sit 'between' your legs rather than back.
Drive straight up, leading with your elbows to prevent dumping the bar forward.
tips: Requires significant thoracic mobility.
Isolates the quads more than back squats and places less shear force on the lumbar spine.

description: A squat variation that emphasizes the quadriceps and upper back posture.

name: Leg Press

instructions.setup: Sit in the machine with back flat against the pad. Place feet shoulder-width on the platform.
execution: Lower the platform until your legs form a 90-degree angle (or slightly deeper if mobility allows).
Press the weight back up.
Do NOT lock your knees at the top.
tips: Ensure your lower back stays glued to the pad; if your butt lifts (butt wink), you are going too deep.
High foot placement biases glutes/hams; low placement biases quads.

description: Allows for heavy loading of the legs without the spinal compression of squats.

name: Machine Hack Squat

instructions.setup: Position shoulders under pads and feet on the platform.
execution: Descend deep, allowing the knees to travel forward over the toes.
Drive through the whole foot to return to the top.
Keep the back flat against the pad.
tips: One of the best exercises for sweeping quad development.
Often safer to train to failure here than with free weights.

description: A guided squat movement that stabilizes the back, allowing for maximum quad isolation.

name: Forward Lunge

instructions.setup: Stand tall with dumbbells in hand.
execution: Step forward significantly.
Lower hips until both knees are at 90 degrees.
Push off the FRONT foot explosively to return to start.
tips: Requires deceleration, placing higher stress on the knees than reverse lunges.
Keep the torso upright.

description: A dynamic movement emphasizing the quads and deceleration mechanics.

name: Reverse Lunge

instructions.setup: Stand tall.
execution: Step backward.
Lower the back knee towards the floor.
Drive through the FRONT heel to pull yourself back to the standing position.
tips: Generally safer for the knees than forward lunges.
Allows for a greater hip angle, increasing glute recruitment.

description: A stable unilateral exercise often preferred for knee health.

name: Lateral Lunge

instructions.setup: Stand with feet wide or start together.
execution: Step out to the side (or shift weight to one side).
Keep the trailing leg completely straight.
Push hips back and bend the working knee.
Push off the bent leg to return to center.
tips: Crucial for frontal plane movement (side-to-side), which is often neglected.
Keep the heel of the working foot flat.

description: Targets the inner thigh and glute medius, improving lateral stability.

name: Romanian Deadlift

instructions.setup: Start from the top (standing) holding the weight.
execution: Unlock knees slightly (soft bend) and keep them fixed there.
Push your hips backward as far as possible while sliding the weight down your legs.
Stop when your hips stop moving back (usually mid-shin).
Squeeze glutes to thrust hips forward to standing.
tips: Movement is horizontal (hips back), not vertical (squatting down).
Keep the bar in contact with your legs to protect the lower back.

description: The gold standard for hamstring hypertrophy and hip hinge mechanics.

name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift

instructions.setup: Start with bar on the floor. Hips are higher than in a conventional deadlift. Legs are nearly straight.
execution: Pull the weight up using a pure hip hinge.
Lower the bar all the way to the floor (dead stop) between reps.
Maintain a neutral spine, though some rounding of the upper back is common.
tips: Biases the hamstrings through lengthening.
Often allows for greater range of motion than RDL but requires more flexibility.

description: A pulling movement starting from a dead stop that places maximum stretch on the hamstrings.

name: Leg Extension

instructions.setup: Adjust seat so your knee aligns with the machine pivot.
execution: Extend legs until knees are locked out.
Squeeze quads hard at the top.
Lower under control.
tips: The only exercise that loads the rectus femoris in its shortened position.
Avoid jerking the weight to protect knee ligaments.

description: Isolates the quadriceps, specifically helpful for finishing off the legs after compounds.

name: Seated Leg Curl

instructions.setup: Lock the lap pad down tight against your thighs.
execution: Curl the weight down and back as far as possible.
Control the return to the stretch position.
tips: Research suggests seated curls are superior to lying curls for hypertrophy due to the stretched position of the hamstrings at the hip.
Do not lift your body out of the seat.

description: Isolates the hamstrings in a lengthened position.

name: Lying Leg Curl

instructions.setup: Lie face down. Knee pivot aligns with machine pivot.
execution: Curl heels towards glutes.
Squeeze hard.
Lower slowly.
tips: Keep your hips pressed into the bench; if they rise, you are using your lower back.
Works the hamstrings in a more shortened position.

description: A staple isolation movement for the posterior chain.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust

instructions.setup: Sit on floor with upper back against a bench. Roll bar over hips (use a pad).
execution: Drive through heels to extend hips vertically.
Fully lock out hips at the top (posterior pelvic tilt).
Chin tucked, eyes forward.
Lower hips back to floor.
tips: If you feel it in your lower back, you are likely hyperextending the spine rather than extending the hips.
Keep shins vertical at the top.

description: The most effective loaded exercise for isolating and building the glutes.

name: Seated Calf Raise

instructions.setup: Sit with pads over lower thighs.
execution: Lower heels fully.
Raise heels fully.
tips: Because the knees are bent, the Gastrocnemius is slack, forcing the Soleus (underlying muscle) to do the work.
Crucial for calf width.

description: Targets the soleus muscle, which lies underneath the gastrocnemius.

name: Adductor Machine

instructions.setup: Sit with pads on the INSIDE of knees.
execution: Squeeze legs together.
Pause at the center.
Return slowly to stretch.
tips: Essential for injury prevention (groin strains) and stabilizing squats.
Don't go so wide in the stretch that you feel pain.

description: Isolates the inner thigh muscles.

name: Abductor Machine

instructions.setup: Sit with pads on the OUTSIDE of knees.
execution: Push legs outward against resistance.
Focus on using the glutes to drive the movement.
tips: Targets the Glute Medius/Minimus.
Lean forward slightly to increase glute recruitment.

description: Targets the outer hip muscles responsible for stabilization and aesthetics.

name: Goblet Squat

instructions.setup: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell against your chest with both hands (goblet hold).
execution: Squat down (between your legs).
Keep elbows inside knees at the bottom.
Drive back up.
tips: The front load acts as a counterbalance, making it easier to hit depth with good form.
Excellent teaching tool for squat mechanics.

description: A user-friendly squat variation that naturally enforces good posture and depth.

name: Step-Up

instructions.setup: Place one foot entirely on a box/bench (knee should be roughly 90 degrees).
execution: Drive through the boxed foot to lift the body up.
Do not push off the floor with the trailing leg.
Stand tall, then lower slowly.
tips: A higher box biases the glutes; a lower box biases the quads.
Control the descent; don't just drop.

description: A functional unilateral movement that challenges balance and single-leg strength.

name: Barbell Curl

instructions.setup: Stand tall holding a barbell with a shoulder-width underhand grip.
execution: Keep elbows pinned to your sides.
Curl the bar up towards your chest.
Squeeze biceps hard at the top.
Lower under control to full extension.
tips: Do not swing the hips to cheat the weight up.
Keep the wrists straight; do not curl the wrists at the top.

description: The standard mass builder for the biceps, allowing for the heaviest loading.

name: Dumbbell Curl

instructions.setup: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides, palms facing your legs (neutral).
execution: Curl the weights up.
As you pass the thigh, rotate (supinate) your palms so they face the ceiling.
Squeeze at the top.
Rotate back to neutral on the way down.
tips: Supination (twisting the wrist) is a primary function of the biceps; emphasize this twist.
Can be done alternating or both arms at once.

description: Allows for separate arm training and maximal bicep contraction via supination.

name: Preacher Curl

instructions.setup: Sit on the preacher bench. Adjust height so armpits rest comfortably over the pad.
execution: Lower the bar until arms are fully extended.
Curl the weight up.
Stop just before the forearms are vertical to maintain tension.
tips: Offers a strict movement that prevents body momentum.
Be careful not to hyperextend elbows at the bottom with heavy weights.

description: Isolates the biceps by stabilizing the upper arm, focusing on the short head.

name: Hammer Curl

instructions.setup: Stand holding dumbbells with palms facing your body.
execution: Curl the weight up while keeping palms facing each other (neutral grip).
Do not rotate the wrist.
Lower under control.
tips: Targets the Brachialis (pushes the bicep up) and Brachioradialis (forearm).
Great for adding thickness to the arm.

description: A bicep curl variation performed with a neutral grip to target the outer arm and forearm.

name: Concentration Curl

instructions.setup: Sit on a bench. Rest the back of your upper arm against your inner thigh.
execution: Curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder.
Squeeze firmly at the peak.
Lower slowly without lifting the arm off the thigh.
tips: Prevents any shoulder involvement or swinging.
Focus on the 'peak' of the bicep.

description: A strict isolation movement that removes all momentum, focusing on the peak contraction.

name: Spider Curl

instructions.setup: Lie chest-down on an incline bench set to 45 degrees. Arms hang straight down.
execution: Curl the bar up without moving your elbows forward or backward.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower fully.
tips: Gravity provides maximum resistance at the point of peak contraction.
Ensure the shoulders stay relaxed.

description: Targets the short head of the biceps with elbows positioned in front of the body.

name: Skull Crusher

instructions.setup: Lie on a flat bench. Hold bar directly above chest.
execution: Bend at the elbows to lower the bar towards your forehead (or slightly behind head).
Keep elbows pointing at the ceiling.
Extend arms back to the starting position.
tips: Lowering the bar behind the head (rather than to the forehead) increases long-head recruitment and saves elbows.
Keep elbows tucked in.

description: A staple tricep exercise that places high tension on the muscle during the stretch.

name: Overhead Tricep Extension (DB)

instructions.setup: Sit (or stand) holding one dumbbell with both hands overhead.
execution: Lower the weight behind your head by bending elbows.
Get a deep stretch in the triceps.
Press the weight back up to full extension.
tips: Ideally performed seated to protect the lower back.
Crucial for hitting the 'Long Head' of the triceps.

description: Targets the long head of the triceps by placing the shoulder in flexion.

name: Overhead Tricep Extension (Cable)

instructions.setup: Set pulley to low (or high if leaning forward). Grab rope and turn away from machine.
execution: Extend arms overhead.
Bend elbows to lower rope behind head.
Extend arms forward/upward.
tips: Constant tension from the cable makes this superior to dumbbells for some.
Keep core tight to avoid arching back.

description: Cable variation of the overhead extension providing consistent resistance.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press

instructions.setup: Lie on bench. Grip bar shoulder-width apart (hands aligned with shoulders).
execution: Unrack and lower bar to lower chest.
Keep elbows tucked close to the torso.
Press back up explosively.
tips: Do not go too narrow (hands touching), as this strains wrists without adding benefit.
The heavy loading capability makes this the best mass builder for triceps.

description: A compound movement that shifts the emphasis of the bench press from chest to triceps.

name: Tricep Dips

instructions.setup: Mount dip bars with arms straight.
execution: Keep torso UPRIGHT (do not lean forward).
Lower body until elbows are at 90 degrees.
Press back up, focusing on extending the elbows.
tips: If you lean forward, you recruit the chest; stay vertical for triceps.
Keep elbows tucked in, not flared out.

description: Bodyweight compound exercise emphasizing the triceps via vertical torso positioning.

name: Reverse Curl

instructions.setup: Hold bar with an overhand (pronated) grip, shoulder-width apart.
execution: Curl the weight up using the tops of your forearms.
Keep wrists straight or slightly extended.
Lower slowly.
tips: Primary target is the Brachioradialis and wrist extensors.
Use an EZ bar if a straight bar hurts your wrists.

description: Targets the forearm extensors and the brachialis muscle.

name: Wrist Curl

instructions.setup: Sit on bench. Rest forearms on thighs with wrists hanging off knees, palms up.
execution: Allow the weight to roll down into your fingers.
Curl the wrist upward as high as possible.
Squeeze the forearm flexors.
tips: Use high reps.
Do not use the biceps to lift the weight; isolate the wrist.

description: Directly isolates the wrist flexor muscles on the underside of the forearm.

name: Zottman Curl

instructions.setup: Stand with dumbbells at sides.
execution: Phase 1: Curl up with palms facing up (standard curl).
Phase 2: At the top, rotate wrists 180 degrees so palms face down.
Phase 3: Lower the weight slowly with the overhand grip (reverse curl).
Rotate back to start at the bottom.
tips: Hits the biceps on the concentric (way up) and forearms on the eccentric (way down).
Control the negative portion; that is the key to this exercise.

description: A hybrid curl that targets both the biceps and the forearms in a single rep.

name: Rope Pushdown

instructions.setup: Attach rope to high pulley. Grip ends with neutral grip.
execution: Start with elbows bent at 90 degrees by your sides.
Push the rope down until arms are fully extended.
Pull the rope ends APART at the bottom for peak contraction.
tips: Keep elbows pinned to your ribs; do not let them drift forward.
Separating the rope maximizes the contraction of the lateral head.

description: An isolation exercise focusing on the lateral head of the tricep and peak contraction.

name: Kneeling Cable Crunch

instructions.setup: Kneel facing the cable stack. Hold the rope behind your head/neck.
execution: Keeping your hips fixed (do not sit back onto your heels), curl your spine downwards.
Imagine trying to bring your forehead to your knees.
Squeeze the abs hard at the bottom.
Uncurl slowly to the starting position.
tips: If your hips move back and forth, you are using your weight to pull, not your abs.
Round the back; keeping a straight back disengages the abs and uses hip flexors.

description: One of the few weighted ab exercises allowing for progressive overload.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout

instructions.setup: Kneel on a pad. Hold the wheel with both hands directly under shoulders.
execution: Roll the wheel forward, extending your body as far as you can without arching your back.
Maintain a slight posterior pelvic tilt (tucked tailbone) throughout.
Use your abs and lats to pull yourself back to the start.
tips: If you feel this in your lower back, you have lost core tension; reduce the range of motion.
Think of it as an 'Anti-Extension' exercise.

description: An advanced anti-extension exercise that builds significant core stability.

name: Russian Twist

instructions.setup: Sit on floor, lean torso back 45 degrees, and lift feet off the floor (balancing on glutes).
execution: Holding a weight, rotate your torso from side to side.
Touch the weight to the floor on each side.
Follow the weight with your eyes/head.
tips: Move the shoulders, not just the arms.
If lower back hurts, put feet down on the floor.

description: A rotational core exercise that targets the obliques and balance.

name: Dragon Flag

instructions.setup: Lie on a bench. Grip the edge of the bench firmly behind your head.
execution: Lift your entire body (legs and torso) up until nearly vertical, resting only on upper back.
Keep the body rigid (straight line).
Lower the entire body slowly as a single unit without breaking at the hips.
tips: This is an extreme anti-extension exercise.
Do not attempt if you have lower back issues.

description: Legendary core exercise popularized by Bruce Lee, requiring immense total body tension.

name: Decline Sit-Up

instructions.setup: Secure legs in a decline bench.
execution: Lie back fully.
Contract abs to curl the torso up towards knees.
Lower under control.
tips: Place hands across chest for easier difficulty, or behind head for harder.
Avoid pulling on the neck.

description: Increases the range of motion and gravity leverage compared to floor sit-ups.

name: Cable Woodchopper

instructions.setup: Set pulley to high (high-to-low) or low (low-to-high). Stand sideways.
execution: Grab handle with both hands.
Rotate torso explosively away from the machine, pivoting the back foot.
Return slowly to the start resisting the pull.
tips: Power comes from the hips and torso rotation, not just arm swinging.
Keep arms relatively straight.

description: A functional rotational power exercise that mimics real-world throwing or swinging patterns.

name: Dead Bug

instructions.setup: Lie on back with arms extended to ceiling and legs in tabletop (90 degrees).
execution: Press lower back FIRMLY into the floor (flatten the gap).
Slowly extend opposite arm and opposite leg toward the floor.
Return to center and switch sides.
Never let the lower back peel off the floor.
tips: If the back arches, you have failed the rep.
Exhale hard as you extend limbs to brace the core.

description: The best exercise for learning how to dissociate limb movement from spine stability.

name: Bird Dog

instructions.setup: Start on hands and knees (quadruped position), spine neutral.
execution: Extend opposite arm and opposite leg straight out.
Pause and hold stability without shifting hips.
Return to start and switch.
tips: Imagine balancing a glass of water on your lower back; don't spill it.
Great for spinal health and coordination.

description: A rehabilitative and stability exercise for the posterior chain and core.

name: Assault Bike

instructions.setup: Adjust seat height so leg is nearly straight at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
execution: Pedal hard with legs while simultaneously pushing and pulling the handles.
Coordinate the rhythm: as one leg kicks down, the opposite arm pushes forward.
Maintain an upright torso.
tips: Do not let the arms go limp; the 'push-pull' of the upper body significantly increases calorie burn.
Use for high-intensity interval training (HIIT).

description: A full-body conditioning tool where resistance increases as you pedal faster.

name: Concept 2 Rower

instructions.setup: Secure feet in straps. Grab handle.
execution: Sequence: Legs push, hips hinge back, arms pull.
Return: Arms extend, hips hinge forward, legs bend.
Drive powerfully through the heels.
tips: 60% legs, 30% core, 10% arms. Do not pull with arms early.
Keep the damper setting reasonable (3-5 is standard for water simulation).

description: A low-impact, high-output posterior chain endurance exercise.

name: Treadmill Incline Walk

instructions.setup: Set treadmill to max incline (usually 12-15%) and a moderate walking speed (3-4 km/h).
execution: Walk with long strides.
Do NOT hold the handrails.
Keep torso upright; do not lean forward into the console.
tips: Holding the rails leans your body back, effectively making the incline 0% relative to your body angle.
Excellent for Zone 2 heart rate training.

description: Low impact steady state (LISS) cardio that specifically targets the posterior chain due to the incline.

name: Stairmaster

instructions.setup: Step onto the machine and select level.
execution: Climb the rotating stairs.
Press through the heel to engage glutes.
Avoid leaning your entire bodyweight on the arm supports.
tips: Leaning on the console reduces calorie burn by up to 30%.
Take deep steps (skipping a step) to bias glutes more.

description: Simulates continuous stair climbing, providing a potent stimulus for legs and heart rate.

name: Battle Ropes

instructions.setup: Stand in a quarter squat holding rope ends. Leave some slack.
execution: Create waves by rapidly raising and lowering arms (alternating or double whip).
Keep the core braced tightly to prevent torso swaying.
Maintain rhythm for time.
tips: It's not just an arm workout; use your legs and hips to generate power.
Great finisher for shoulder endurance.

description: High-intensity metabolic conditioning tool focusing on upper body power output.

name: Jump Rope

instructions.setup: Hold handles with elbows tucked in.
execution: Flick wrists to rotate rope (do not use big arm circles).
Bounce lightly on the balls of your feet.
Clear the rope by only an inch or two.
tips: Stay relaxed; tension causes fatigue.
Improves footwork, coordination, and bone density.

description: Classic conditioning exercise developing coordination, ankle stiffness, and cardiovascular endurance.

name: Downward-Facing Dog

instructions.setup: Start on hands and knees, hands slightly forward of shoulders.
execution: Lift knees away from floor, reaching tailbone toward the ceiling.
Straighten legs without locking knees and press heels toward the floor.
Press firmly through palms and knuckles, keeping ears aligned with upper arms.
tips: Rotate inner elbows forward to engage the shoulders.
Keep the spine long rather than focusing on flat heels.

description: A foundational yoga pose that provides a full-body stretch and builds shoulder stability.

name: World's Greatest Stretch

instructions.setup: Step into a deep lunge with the back knee off the ground.
execution: Place the hand opposite the front foot on the ground.
Rotate the torso, reaching the arm closest to the front foot toward the sky.
Bring the elbow of the reaching arm down toward the instep of the front foot.
tips: Keep the back leg active and straight.
Follow your hand with your eyes to maximize thoracic rotation.

description: A comprehensive mobility drill targeting the hips, spine, and shoulders in one movement.

name: Pigeon Pose

instructions.setup: From a plank or downward dog, bring one knee forward toward the same-side wrist.
execution: Place the shin on the floor, aiming to keep it parallel to the front of the mat.
Extend the back leg straight behind you, hips squared to the floor.
Lower the torso over the front leg as comfort permits.
tips: Flex the front foot to protect the knee joint.
Use a block under the glute if hips are tight.

description: An intense hip-opening pose targeting the gluteus muscles and deep hip rotators.

name: Skater Jumps

instructions.setup: Stand in a small semi-squat position.
execution: Jump laterally to the right, landing on the right foot with a soft knee.
Sweep the left leg behind the right and swing arms across the body.
Immediately jump back to the left, repeating the motion.
tips: Maintain a low center of gravity.
Focus on distance and control rather than just speed.

description: A lateral plyometric exercise that builds side-to-side power and ankle stability.

name: 90/90 Hip Switch

instructions.setup: Sit on the floor with knees bent at 90 degrees, one leg in front and one to the side.
execution: Keeping feet on the floor, rotate the knees to the opposite side.
Maintain an upright torso without using hands for support if possible.
Pause in the end range to feel the internal and external rotation.
tips: Try to keep the spine as vertical as possible.
Drive the knees toward the floor actively.

description: Improves internal and external hip rotation, essential for squat depth and lower back health.

name: Cat-Cow

instructions.setup: Start on all fours in a tabletop position.
execution: Inhale, drop the belly, and look up (Cow).
Exhale, round the spine, and tuck the chin (Cat).
Flow between positions following the breath.
tips: Initiate movement from the pelvis.
Avoid collapsing into the shoulders.

description: A gentle flow to improve spinal flexibility and core awareness.

name: Broad Jump

instructions.setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart.
execution: Hinge hips back and swing arms backward.
Explode forward as far as possible, swinging arms for momentum.
Land on both feet, absorbing impact through hips and knees.
tips: Do not land with locked knees.
Focus on horizontal distance.

description: Develops explosive horizontal power and lower body coordination.

name: Warrior II

instructions.setup: Stand with feet wide apart, right foot facing forward and left foot turned 90 degrees.
execution: Bend the right knee so it is directly over the ankle.
Extend arms parallel to the floor, palms down.
Gaze over the right hand, keeping the torso centered.
tips: Keep the back leg engaged and straight.
Do not let the front knee cave inward.

description: A standing pose that builds leg strength, endurance, and hip flexibility.

name: Thoracic Bridge

instructions.setup: Sit with feet flat and hands behind you, like a crab walk position.
execution: Lift the hips and reach one arm diagonally over the opposite shoulder.
Rotate the torso to look at the ground while driving the hips high.
Return to center and switch sides.
tips: Push the ground away with the supporting hand.
Drive through the heels to engage the glutes.

description: Combines glute activation with significant thoracic spine and shoulder mobilization.

name: Cobra Pose

instructions.setup: Lie face down with hands under the shoulders.
execution: Press the tops of the feet into the mat.
Inhale and lift the chest off the floor using back strength.
Keep the elbows close to the body and shoulders down.
tips: Don't use only arm strength; focus on the back.
Keep the neck neutral.

description: A heart-opening backbend that strengthens the spine and stretches the chest.

name: Tuck Jumps

instructions.setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart.
execution: Jump vertically as high as possible.
Pull the knees toward the chest at the peak of the jump.
Land softly and immediately prepare for the next rep.
tips: Focus on a quick ground contact time.
Land on the balls of the feet.

description: An advanced plyometric move that requires high power output and core engagement.

name: Child's Pose

instructions.setup: Kneel on the floor, big toes touching, sitting on your heels.
execution: Separate your knees hip-width or wider.
Fold forward, resting your forehead on the floor.
Extend arms forward or rest them alongside the body.
tips: Breathe into the back of the ribs.
Use a block for the forehead if the floor is too far.

description: A restorative pose used to calm the nervous system and stretch the back.

name: Scapular Wall Slides

instructions.setup: Stand with back, head, and glutes against a wall.
execution: Place arms in a 'goalpost' position against the wall.
Slide arms upward while keeping elbows and wrists in contact with the wall.
Lower back down with control, squeezing the shoulder blades.
tips: Keep the lower back pressed against the wall.
Don't shrug the shoulders.

description: Corrects posture and improves scapular upward rotation and stability.

name: Boat Pose

instructions.setup: Sit with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
execution: Lean back slightly and lift feet off the floor.
Straighten the legs to form a 'V' shape with the body.
Extend arms forward, parallel to the floor.
tips: Keep the chest lifted and spine long.
Bend knees if the lower back rounds.

description: A core-strengthening pose that challenges balance and hip flexor endurance.

name: Depth Jumps

instructions.setup: Stand on top of a box (12-24 inches).
execution: Step off the box, landing on both feet.
Immediately upon contact, jump as high as possible.
Minimize time spent on the ground.
tips: Do not jump off the box; step off.
Focus on reactive speed.

description: Utilizes the stretch-shortening cycle to maximize reactive power.

name: Shoulder Dislocations

instructions.setup: Hold a PVC pipe with a very wide grip.
execution: With straight arms, bring the pipe over the head and down to the lower back.
Reverse the movement back to the starting position.
Gradually narrow the grip as mobility improves.
tips: Keep the elbows locked.
Don't arch the lower back.

description: Improves shoulder range of motion and joint health.

name: Triangle Pose

instructions.setup: Stand with wide legs, right foot out and left foot slightly in.
execution: Reach the right arm forward, then down to the shin or a block.
Extend the left arm toward the ceiling.
Keep both sides of the torso long and gaze upward.
tips: Don't collapse into the lower hand.
Keep the body in one plane as if between two panes of glass.

description: Stretches the hamstrings and groins while strengthening the core.

name: Plyometric Push-Ups

instructions.setup: Start in a standard push-up position.
execution: Lower the chest to the floor.
Push up with enough force that the hands leave the ground.
Land softly and transition into the next rep.
tips: Keep the core tight to prevent hip sagging.
Start on knees to build power if needed.

description: Develops explosive power in the upper body pushing muscles.

name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Stretch

instructions.setup: Stand facing a wall in a staggered stance.
execution: Drive the front knee toward the wall without lifting the heel.
Pulse forward and back to increase the range.
Move the foot further back as mobility increases.
tips: Keep the heel glued to the floor.
Ensure the knee tracks over the toes.

description: Essential for squat mechanics and preventing lower limb injuries.

name: Medicine Ball Slams

instructions.setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a ball.
execution: Reach the ball overhead, extending the body.
Slam the ball into the floor as hard as possible, following through with hips.
Catch the ball on the bounce or pick it up and repeat.
tips: Use the core to generate the power, not just arms.
Keep a flat back.

description: Develops explosive core power and metabolic conditioning.

name: Thread the Needle

instructions.setup: Start on all fours.
execution: Reach one arm under the opposite arm, resting the shoulder on the floor.
Keep hips stacked over the knees.
Extend the other arm forward or wrap it around the back.
tips: Breathe into the stretch between the shoulder blades.
Do not force the shoulder down.

description: A relaxing stretch that improves thoracic rotation and shoulder mobility.

name: Split Squat Jumps

instructions.setup: Start in a lunge position.
execution: Jump explosively upward.
Switch leg positions in mid-air.
Land softly in a lunge with the opposite foot forward.
tips: Maintain an upright torso.
Focus on vertical height.

description: Builds explosive power and unilateral leg stability.

name: Tree Pose

instructions.setup: Stand on one leg.
execution: Place the sole of the other foot on the inner calf or thigh.
Avoid the knee joint.
Bring hands to heart center or reach them overhead.
tips: Find a focal point (Drishti) for balance.
Press the foot and thigh into each other.

description: Improves balance, focus, and ankle strength.

name: Jefferson Curl

instructions.setup: Stand on a bench or floor with light weight.
execution: Slowly tuck the chin and roll down one vertebra at a time.
Keep legs straight as you reach the weight toward or below the feet.
Slowly roll back up to a standing position.
tips: Use very light weight to start.
Movement should be slow and controlled.

description: Develops spinal articulation and extreme posterior chain flexibility.

name: Crow Pose

instructions.setup: Squat down and place hands flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
execution: Place knees high up on the back of the triceps.
Lean forward, shifting weight into the hands until feet lift.
Squeeze the inner thighs and pull the navel in.
tips: Look forward, not down at your feet.
Spread fingers wide for a stable base.

description: An introductory arm balance that builds core and wrist strength.

name: Sphinx Pose

instructions.setup: Lie on your stomach with elbows under the shoulders.
execution: Forearms are parallel on the floor.
Press into the elbows to lift the chest.
Lengthen the tailbone toward the heels.
tips: Keep the neck long and shoulders away from ears.
Engage the glutes slightly to protect the lower back.

description: A gentle backbend ideal for counteracting a seated posture.

name: Scorpion Stretch

instructions.setup: Lie face down with arms out in a 'T' shape.
execution: Lift the left leg and reach the foot toward the right hand.
Keep the right shoulder in contact with the floor.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Move slowly to avoid straining the spine.
Focus on the chest and hip stretch.

description: A dynamic stretch for the anterior chain and spinal rotation.

name: Bridge Pose

instructions.setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
execution: Lift the hips toward the ceiling.
Interlace hands under the back and roll the shoulders underneath.
Keep the thighs parallel.
tips: Don't let the knees splay outward.
Press into the heels.

description: Strengthens the posterior chain and opens the chest and hips.

name: Lateral Bounds

instructions.setup: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend.
execution: Jump laterally to the other leg as far as possible.
Land and stabilize immediately before jumping back.
Use the arms to assist the power.
tips: Focus on 'sticking' the landing.
Maintain a neutral spine.

description: Builds lateral power and joint stability in the ankles and knees.

name: Deep Squat Hold

instructions.setup: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width.
execution: Squat down as deep as possible while keeping heels on the floor.
Use the elbows to push the knees outward.
Keep the chest upright and spine long.
tips: If heels lift, use a wedge or hold onto a pole.
Spend 1-2 minutes here for best results.

description: The ultimate hip and ankle mobility restorative position.

name: Warrior I

instructions.setup: From a lunge, turn the back heel down at a 45-degree angle.
execution: Square the hips toward the front of the mat.
Bend the front knee to 90 degrees.
Reach arms toward the ceiling, palms facing.
tips: Press through the outer edge of the back foot.
Pull the lower ribs in to engage the core.

description: A powerful standing pose that stretches the hip flexors and strengthens the legs.

name: Single-Leg Hops

instructions.setup: Stand on one leg.
execution: Jump vertically using only one leg.
Land softly on the ball of the foot.
Repeat for reps before switching sides.
tips: Keep ground contact time minimal.
